topic: KEEP: writing a three-item Keep List from last month's statement, so you protect what's worth it before you cut anything
pillar: KEEP: deciding what is worth keeping on purpose (the Worth-It Rule: protect what's worth it first), without guilt.
caption:
Before you cut anything, write down what stays.
Grab last month's statement and an index card.
Star the things that made your life better, then pick up to three.
Write one plain reason next to each. That card is your Keep List, and it is allowed to include flowers.
Save this for a quiet twenty minutes this week.
The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is in my link in bio if you want everything on one page.

slides.title: Write your Keep List before you cut a thing
slides.subtitle: A 20-minute Worth-It Rule step

slides.title: Protect what's worth it first
slides.body: Before you cut anything, decide what stays. A Keep List is a short note of the things you pay for on purpose. You need one statement and about twenty minutes.

slides.title: What you need
items: Last month's bank or card statement
A pen and an index card, or the notes app on your phone

slides.title: Find your keeps
items: Read the statement line by line, slowly
Put a small star next to anything that made your life better
Ask yourself: would I choose this again today?
Pick up to three stars to keep on purpose

slides.title: Write one reason next to each keep
slides.body: Example with made-up numbers: Gym, 30 dollars a month. Reason: I sleep better. One plain sentence is enough. The reason is what makes it a keep.

slides.title: Guilt gets no vote on this list
slides.body: A keep can be small and a little silly. Fresh flowers count. So does the show you fall asleep to. If it is worth it to you, it goes on the card.

slides.title: Put the card where you will see it
slides.body: Tape it inside a kitchen cabinet or pin the note on your phone. When you get to Cut later, these three are already protected.

slides.title: Keep this for your next quiet twenty minutes
slides.body: Save this post so it is here when you are ready. If you want your Three Numbers on one page, the free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is in my link in bio. Day one counts.
